Background checks, push from Proxmox, what to notify about

ProxCtrl can check your servers in the background and tell you when something needs attention. Push from Proxmox adds instant notifications for backups, updates and cluster events. Both stay between your phone, your servers and your own ntfy server.
Notifications are turned off for ProxCtrl.
Looks at every saved server and notifies about new problems

Android runs background checks at most every 15 minutes, and can delay them to save battery. CPU and memory are judged from the node\'s own per-minute graphs, so a longer interval doesn\'t miss a high period, it only reports it later.
Last check %1$s couldn\'t reach the server
Through the ntfy app and your own ntfy server
ntfy isn\'t installed. Push from Proxmox comes only through the ntfy app: install it, connect it to your ntfy server, then come back here. Background checks work without it.
ntfy temporarily unavailable: its server can\'t be reached. The push address stays the same and background checks keep running.
ntfy couldn\'t register ProxCtrl (%1$s). Open ntfy once, then try again.
Treat this address like a password: anyone who has it can send you notifications.

Run these commands in your node\'s shell (as root) to send backup failures, updates, fencing, replication and system mail (ZFS and SMART) to ProxCtrl. The last command sends a test notification. The README explains each step.
While push is on, backup failures and updates come from Proxmox, so the background check doesn\'t notify about them twice.
Disk and memory levels are set under Settings › Warnings and are the same as on the Overview.
ProxCtrl may run in the background
Battery optimisation can delay or skip checks
Android can cut ntfy\'s connection while the phone sleeps, so Proxmox notifications arrive late. Tap to open ntfy\'s app info and set Battery to Unrestricted.

On ColorOS and other phones that close background apps aggressively: open ProxCtrl\'s app info, then under Battery choose Allow background activity (or Don\'t optimise), and allow Auto launch if your phone has it. Push from Proxmox keeps working as long as ntfy is allowed to run in the background.

pveproxy, pvedaemon, corosync and the other Proxmox services
Restart the node; all guests are shut down first

Every running guest on the node is shut down or stopped, and the node restarts. Guests set to start on boot come back afterwards; the others stay off. ProxCtrl loses its connection until the node is back.
Turn the node off; all guests are shut down first
Every running guest on the node is shut down or stopped, and the node powers off. Nothing on it can be reached until it\'s turned on again.
You can turn it on again from ProxCtrl with Wake-on-LAN, from the same network.
Wake-on-LAN isn\'t set up in ProxCtrl, so you\'ll need to turn the node on by hand.
If it\'s turned off, wake it with Wake-on-LAN. Your phone has to be on the same network as the node.
If it\'s turned off, ProxCtrl can wake it with Wake-on-LAN once you enter the node\'s MAC address.

ProxCtrl sends a Wake-on-LAN packet from your phone. It only reaches the node when your phone is on the same network, and Wake-on-LAN has to be turned on in the node\'s BIOS or UEFI and for its network card.
The node\'s network card, as shown by ip link on the node
Enter six pairs of hex digits, like AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF
255.255.255.255 and port 9 work on most home networks. Use your network\'s broadcast address (for example 192.168.1.255) if the packet doesn\'t arrive.
